_about: W2-GATHER rare results and butcher yield scaling. Owned by game/scripts/gather/. Every item id must exist in items.json and every tier name in ProgressionScaling.TOOL_TIERS (t_gather checks). Every gather pass gives exactly one item (ONEGATHER). Chances are per gathered item (rare_trait), per gathered pass (gather_rare finds) or per carcass (butcher).
_assumption: The docs set one gather rarity: world-design.md:55 'Every material stamped with attributes: always climate and level; ... 5% chance of a rare extra (green pip)' and PRD:541 'Rare extra attributes = green pip, low chance' (rare_trait, the green traits of spec 04:11). Finds are a node's secondary materials (spec 12:38 'material drop tables'; 12:39 'a tree may yield leaf, branch, log, fruit, sap, or specialized material'). ASSUMPTION: the find odds are illustrative, about one per 20-30 passes.

rare_trait._doc: world-design.md:55, PRD:541: each gathered item has this chance of one green rare trait; spec 04:11 names the six. Spec 12:42: Gathering level never raises it. Keys are INVUI's inv_ui.json attribute_classes of class rare, value true.
rare_trait._assumption: ASSUMPTION: the docs do not say which trait a material gets, so each of the six is equally likely on any gathered material (tool tier scales the 5% since ONEGATHER, see _tool_tier_bonus). RAREATTR narrows that: a material rolls only from by_material[item], its own list, and traits stays the shared fallback for an item with no list (an id added to a node's harvest before its row here).
rare_trait._tool_tier_bonus: ONEGATHER (owner 2026-10-28: 'cap it to 1 per harvest and upgrades can change the speed and quality of the materials you harvest, not the amount'). ASSUMPTION: a gathering tool's material tier is the quality lever: each tier above stone raises a unit's rare-trait odds by 15% of the base (the old count multiplier's tier step, gather_rare's tool_tier_bonus), so a steel tool rolls 5% x 2.05 = 10.25%, capped at max_chance. Bare hands and stone keep the documented 5%. Gathering level still never raises it (spec 12:42); level speeds the pass instead.
rare_trait._tier: BAGUI (owner 2026-10-28: 'Perks have tiers now (Beautiful Pattern IV)'). A rolled rare trait's value is its tier, 1-5 (I-V); an old save's true reads as I. ASSUMPTION: from tier I each further step succeeds with tier_step (35%: II 35%, III 12%, IV 4%, V 1.5% of rolls); each tool tier above stone adds tier_step_tool_bonus and each level of the gathering skill tier_step_skill_bonus, capped at tier_step_max. A craft keeps the primary material's tier; a craft's own rare roll uses the same table without tool or skill.
rare_trait._by_material: RAREATTR: each gatherable material's own rare-attribute list (spec 04:33 'rare attributes may pass from a single eligible primary material'). ASSUMPTION, since spec 04:25 names conversions for five of the six: a combat material (stone, ore, metal, crystal, ice, pearl) rolls black_sheen or low_vibration (Vital Strike / Throw Dirt, Sadism / Pain Averse); a tool-shaping material (timber, fibre, cordage) rolls wide_serration or narrow_hook (gathering effects); a workpiece (timber, earth, clay, resin) also rolls split_easily (workstation effects); vivid_inspiration has no documented conversion, so every material can roll it. The 5% chance and its key names are unchanged; a recipe's own rare roll (world/rules.json rare_attribute_chance) still draws from the full six.

lot._doc: HARVESTROLL: every gather pass is its own lot (spec 04 'rolled positive/negative/rare attributes' per instance; Traits_Gathering_Processing_Math 'lots differ in level, quality, defects and rare virtues'). Level: L = max(1, S - width) + min(width, floor((width + 1) * U^gamma)) for node level S (that doc's site roll; a level-50 node yields 45-50, never above). gamma runs from gamma_novice (Gathering 1, bare hands) down by gamma_skill_drop at Gathering 60 and gamma_tool_drop at the top tool tier, so skill and tools favour the top of the band. Signed traits: by the item's first listed category in by_category; one grey trait at negative_chance, one gold trait at positive_chance (never the grey one's opposite) (scaled by tool tier and Gathering, capped), each of magnitude 1..max_magnitude. Items with no category row (food, herbs, treasure) roll only the level.
lot._assumption: ASSUMPTION (HARVESTROLL, logged in docs/vision/WildLandsMMO_Open_Questions.md): width 5 and gammas 1.5/1.0/0.75 are the math doc's illustrative values; 7% is its unapproved candidate gold odds (grey 35%, owner: 96% 'too harsh'); skill bonus 20% relative at Gathering 60 (doc: worker 0-20%), tool bonus 15% per tier above stone (rare_trait's), cap 12%; magnitudes 1-3; which gold/grey traits each category can roll is read off spec 04's trait meanings.
lot._max_perks: PERKCAP (owner 2026-10-28: 'it should really be 1-2 perks on each gathered item max'): green rare + gold + grey together never exceed max_perks on one gathered item; a green trait that lands on a full item replaces its grey one, else it is skipped. Never a trait and its opposite (opposites) on one lot. ASSUMPTION (owner 'too harsh' to 96%): negative_chance 0.35.

gather_rare._skill_bonus: 0 by spec 12 s1: 'never silently grant rare material traits purely for reaching a high level'. Better tools raise the odds (ASSUMPTION); skill level does not.
gather_rare._climates: A find rolls only on a node whose island climate lists it, and every listed climate's materials (data/world/climates.json, docs/design/world-design.md:66-75) contain the item (t_gather checks). A row never rolls on a node whose own harvest (nature_manifest.json) has that item: a find is a different material, never more of the node's yield. A find's min_tool_tier is never below the pick tier a nature node needs for the same item (nature_manifest min_pick_tier, W2-DATA's ladder; t_gather checks), so a find never skips a rung. Home grassland has no find: each of its materials is some home node's own yield, so its rare results are rare_trait only.
gather_rare._dormant: No island in islands.json is snowfield or blue_tropical yet, so the silver_ore and pearl rows cannot roll in the shipped world until those islands exist (t_gather checks each row has a family that grows in one of its climates).

butcher._rare_chance: ASSUMPTION: spec 12 s2 ('Carcass Part Selection, Not Generic Random Loot') unlocks each part by Butchering nodes, tool and Slaughter Ability. Until W2-BUTCHER adds the Slaughter Ability roll, an unlocked rare part still rolls this chance (or the row's own) as its stand-in.
butcher._cut_speed: ASSUMPTION (owner 2026-10-28: one per harvest, upgrades change speed and quality, not the amount): every cut gives exactly one part. Each knife tier above stone makes a cut 15% faster and each Butchering level 1% (the old part-count bonuses, now on speed); a better knife's quality shows as its rare-part odds (rare_tool_tier_bonus).
